context: The binary tree has preorder traversal preorder = [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder traversal inorder = [9, 3, 1, 2, 7]. Its node values are distinct.
Preorder visits root → left subtree → right subtree. Inorder visits left subtree → root → right subtree. Together, the positions in the two sequences uniquely determine the whole tree.
description: The left side shows the tree to reconstruct. Root 3 has left child 9 and right child 2. Node 2 has left child 1 and right child 7. Nodes 9, 1, and 7 are leaves.

On the right, the two traversal sequences are stacked above one another. An arrow labeled “Reconstruct the binary tree” points left toward the tree. The first preorder element, 3, determines the root. Only 9 precedes 3 in inorder, so the left subtree contains just 9. The inorder segment [1, 2, 7] to the right of 3 corresponds to the final preorder segment [2, 1, 7]. Thus the right subtree has root 2 with children 1 and 7.
This is an ordinary binary tree. Its positions follow from the traversal order, without the ordering constraint of a binary search tree. For example, the left child 9 is greater than its parent 3.

frames.explanation: Preorder locates the subtree roots, and inorder identifies the nodes belonging to each subtree. With distinct node values, the two traversals determine a unique tree.
frames.title: Reconstructing a five-node binary tree from preorder and inorder traversals

summary: The preorder sequence [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder sequence [9, 3, 1, 2, 7] uniquely determine a five-node binary tree rooted at 3.
title: Reconstructing a five-node binary tree from preorder and inorder traversals
